subtitle: How a Saka king carved Sanskrit statecraft into living stone

panels.shot: wide, low-angle view of the Girnar rock face looming over rugged land, with Rudradaman I in the foreground, hand resting on the rough stone as if claiming it
panels.action: Rudradaman I stands in regal Saka attire before the weathered Girnar rock, wind whipping his cloak, as the vast stone surface curves away behind him under a stark sky.

dialogue.text: On a worn rock above Girnar, a Saka king dared to make Sanskrit the language of power, and carved a new way for rulers to speak to the world.

i18n.hi: गिरनार की घिसी चट्टान पर एक शक राजा ने हिम्मत की—सत्ता की भाषा संस्कृत, और दुनिया से बात करने का नया ढंग पत्थर में तराश दिया।

panels.shot: close, ground-level view of the ancient rock, showing faint older inscriptions cut into its surface
panels.action: The Girnar rock fills the frame, its curved surface etched with older, weathered lines of Brahmi script, with cracks and lichen hinting at centuries of sun and rain.

dialogue.text: Long before Rudradaman, this very rock had spoken. Ashoka’s Prakrit edicts, cut in an earlier age, still clung to its curve like whispers from the Mauryan past.

i18n.hi: रुद्रदामन से बहुत पहले, यही पत्थर बोल चुका था। अशोक के प्राकृत शिलालेख मौर्यकाल की फुसफुसाहट की तरह इसकी मोड़ पर अब भी चिपके थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Rudradaman I studying the rock, fingers tracing old lines
panels.action: Rudradaman I, middle-aged and broad-shouldered, leans close to the stone, brow furrowed, his fingers hovering over the faint Prakrit lines while attendants stand respectfully behind.

dialogue.text: By the mid-second century, the Mauryans were gone. The Western Kshatrapa Rudradaman, a Saka satrap turned king, now ruled this land and its old imperial stone.

i18n.hi: दूसरी शताब्दी के बीच तक मौर्य जा चुके थे। पश्चिमी क्षत्रप रुद्रदामन, शक क्षत्रप से राजा बने, अब इस देश और इसके पुराने शाही पत्थर के स्वामी थे।

panels.shot: interior court scene, wide shot of Rudradaman on a simple throne in a hall, maps and merchants around
panels.action: In a pillared hall, Rudradaman I sits on a low throne, listening as courtiers gesture over a map of western India with ports and rivers marked, while traders in diverse dress wait with ledgers.

dialogue.text: His realm stretched from the Arabian Sea ports inland to Girnar. Trade with Rome and the Deccan flowed through his harbours, while upland farmers watched the monsoon with anxious eyes.

i18n.hi: उसका राज्य अरबी सागर के बंदरगाहों से भीतर गिरनार तक फैला था। रोम और दक्कन की दौलत उसके बंदरों से बहती, और ऊँचाई के किसान डरते-डरते मानसून ताका करते।

panels.shot: wide shot of a great stone embankment (Sudarsana lake) cracked after floods, villagers and officials inspecting
panels.action: A wide stone embankment at the foot of a rocky hill shows clear damage, with a breached section and dry, cracked reservoir bed, as villagers, officials, and soldiers gather in concern.

dialogue.text: Near Girnar lay the Sudarsana lake, once built under Chandragupta and repaired under Ashoka. A fierce flood had ruined its embankment, threatening fields and lives downstream.

i18n.hi: गिरनार के पास था सुधर्शन झील—कभी चन्द्रगुप्त के समय बनी, फिर अशोक ने सुधारी। भीषण बाढ़ ने बाँध तोड़ दिया, खेतों और नीचे के गाँवों की जान पर बनी।

panels.shot: heroic low-angle shot of Rudradaman addressing engineers and officials at the ruined dam
panels.action: Rudradaman stands on the broken embankment, arm outstretched toward the breach, as engineers with measuring rods and scribes with palm-leaf bundles bow and listen intently.

dialogue.speaker: rudradaman_i
dialogue.text: Rebuild it stronger. Let no farmer curse the rains again.

i18n.hi: इसे और मजबूत बनाओ। फिर कोई किसान बरसात को कोसे नहीं।

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot of reconstruction: workers hauling stone, elephants dragging logs, water channeled
panels.action: Lines of labourers carry shaped stones, elephants haul heavy timbers, and supervisors point as new masonry rises, while channels divert a trickle of water around the worksite.

dialogue.text: The inscription later would say: he rebuilt at his own cost, sparing his subjects forced labour and new taxes. The Sudarsana dam rose again under his order.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख बाद में कहेगा: उसने अपना धन लगा कर बाँध बनाया, प्रजाजनों पर जबरन मेहनत या नए कर नहीं थोपे। सुधर्शन का बाँध फिर उसकी आज्ञा से उठ खड़ा हुआ।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Rudradaman in a quieter setting with scholars, scrolls of Prakrit and Sanskrit around
panels.action: In a shaded verandah, Rudradaman sits with Brahmin scholars, palm-leaf manuscripts spread out; one scroll shows rounded Prakrit letters, another dense Sanskrit text, as he listens keenly.

dialogue.text: Rudradaman was no mere warrior. His own inscription praises him as skilled in grammar, music, and in composing both prose and verse—though whether his hand held the stylus we cannot know.

i18n.hi: रुद्रदामन केवल योद्धा नहीं था। उसका अपना शिलालेख उसे व्याकरण, संगीत और गद्य-पद्य रचने में निपुण बताता है—हालाँकि खुद कलम उसने चलाई या नहीं, यह हम नहीं जान पाते।

panels.shot: medium shot, slight high angle, of Rudradaman and a chief scribe debating, with a palm-leaf draft between them
panels.action: Rudradaman and a chief scribe sit across a low table; between them lies a palm-leaf draft, the scribe gesturing carefully while the king rests his hand thoughtfully on his chin.

dialogue.text: Across India, most royal records still spoke in Prakrit. Yet in his court, Sanskrit—long the language of ritual and learning—grew into something sharper, suited to praise and policy.

i18n.hi: भारत भर में ज़्यादातर शाही लेख अभी भी प्राकृत में थे। पर उसके दरबार में संस्कृत—जो अब तक पूजा और विद्या की भाषा थी—और तेज, और धारदार हुई, प्रशंसा और नीति की ज़ुबान बनी।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot from behind the scribe, showing Rudradaman gesturing toward Girnar on a small map
panels.action: From behind the scribe, we see Rudradaman’s hand resting on a small map where Girnar and the lake are marked, as he points decisively toward the rock’s location.

dialogue.speaker: rudradaman_i
dialogue.text: This stone bears old kings’ words. Let ours stand beside them—in Sanskrit.

i18n.hi: यह पत्थर पुराने राजाओं की वाणी ढोता है। हमारी वाणी भी इनके साथ खड़ी हो—संस्कृत में।

panels.shot: close-up of a palm-leaf manuscript with neat Sanskrit prose, a hand hovering with a stylus
panels.action: A carefully inscribed palm leaf shows flowing Sanskrit prose lines, while a steady hand holding a stylus hovers above, ready to add another sentence.

dialogue.text: The Junagadh text took shape first on leaf and memory: genealogy, victories against Satavahanas and other foes, and the rebuilding of Sudarsana, woven into ornate Sanskrit prose.

i18n.hi: जूनागढ़ लेख पहले पत्ता और स्मृति पर सजा: वंशावली, सातवाहनों और दूसरे शत्रुओं पर विजय, और सुधर्शन के पुनर्निर्माण की कथा, सब सजीली संस्कृत गद्य में गुँथी।

panels.shot: dynamic low-angle shot of artisans at the rock, one reading from a palm-leaf while another chisels
panels.action: At the foot of the Girnar rock, a reciter stands with a palm leaf, slowly chanting as a stone-cutter, kneeling against the stone, chisels each Brahmi letter with focused care; Rudradaman watches from a short distance.

dialogue.text: Then stylus gave way to chisel. Letter by letter, the long Sanskrit prose flowed onto the ancient rock, the first such political inscription we know cut in that learned tongue.

i18n.hi: फिर लेखनी की जगह छैनी ने ली। अक्षर-अक्षर, लंबा संस्कृत गद्य उस प्राचीन पत्थर पर बहता गया—राजनीतिक शिलालेख के रूप में उस विद्वान भाषा का पहला ऐसा नमूना।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of the freshly carved Brahmi letters of the Sanskrit inscription catching the light
panels.action: Newly carved Brahmi characters, still sharp-edged, run in straight lines across the rock face, tiny stone dust clinging to their grooves as late-afternoon light grazes them.

dialogue.text: Its style was new: a prashasti, a royal eulogy in elaborate prose, binding lineage, conquest, and public works into one continuous, crafted voice.

i18n.hi: अंदाज़ भी नया था—प्रशस्ति, सुगठित राजस्तुति, जिसमें वंश, विजय और जनकल्याण एक ही सधे हुए स्वर में बँध गए।

panels.shot: medium wide shot of villagers, traders, and Brahmins gathered below the rock as a court official recites the text
panels.action: A mixed crowd of farmers, merchants, and Brahmins stands below the rock while a court official, scroll in hand, recites upward; Rudradaman stands to the side, arms folded, watching reactions.

dialogue.text: Not all who heard could follow every turn of its Sanskrit. Yet Brahmins, officials, and learned listeners carried its phrases outward, reshaping how rulers’ deeds could be told.

i18n.hi: हर सुनने वाला इसकी हर संस्कृत मोड़ नहीं पकड़ पाया। पर ब्राह्मण, अधिकारी और विद्वान श्रोता इसके वाक्य साथ ले गए, और राजाओं के काम गिनाने की शैली बदलने लगे।

panels.shot: wide, time-lapse style shot suggestion: same rock across ages, faintly overlaying Ashoka’s and Rudradaman’s sections
panels.action: The rock is shown in a timeless wide view, Ashoka’s older lines and Rudradaman’s newer inscription both visible, the hill and sky unchanged as hazy silhouettes of later travelers pass in suggestion.

dialogue.text: Scholars now see this rock as a hinge: Ashoka’s Prakrit morality beside Rudradaman’s Sanskrit statecraft, an old imperial voice answered by a new regional power.

i18n.hi: विद्वान अब इस पत्थर को मोड़ मानते हैं—एक ओर अशोक की प्राकृत नैतिकता, दूसरी ओर रुद्रदामन की संस्कृत राजनीति; पुरानी साम्राज्य-ध्वनि को नई प्रादेशिक शक्ति का जवाब।

panels.shot: interior study scene centuries later: a Gupta-era scribe copying a Sanskrit prashasti by lamplight
panels.action: In a later age, a Gupta scribe sits cross-legged by an oil lamp, carefully copying a richly phrased Sanskrit prashasti onto a fresh palm leaf, stacks of similar texts beside him.

dialogue.text: In centuries to come, Gupta kings and others would fill copper plates and pillars with Sanskrit prashastis, refining the form first fully tried in prose on this Saka king’s stone.

i18n.hi: आने वाली सदियों में गुप्त नरेश और दूसरे राजा ताँबे की ताम्रपट्टियों और स्तंभों को संस्कृत प्रशस्तियों से भर देंगे, उसी रूप को निखारते हुए जो इस शक राजा ने गद्य में पूरी तरह आज़माया।

panels.shot: modern-era wide shot: archaeologists and epigraphists at Girnar, one tracing the inscription with care
panels.action: Modern archaeologists in simple field clothes stand by the Girnar rock; one gently traces a line of the inscription with a gloved hand while another sketches in a notebook.

dialogue.text: Today, epigraphists reading these weathered lines speak of a moment when a foreign-born dynasty made a classical language its own, without erasing the voices that came before.

i18n.hi: आज अभिलेख पढ़ने वाले इन झुलसे अक्षरों में उस घड़ी की बात करते हैं, जब विदेशी मूल के राजवंश ने शास्त्रीय भाषा को अपना बना लिया, बिना पहले की आवाज़ें मिटाए।

panels.shot: reflective medium close-up of Rudradaman looking at the rock at sunset, half in shadow
panels.action: Rudradaman stands again before the rock in the orange light of sunset, his face half lit, half shadowed, eyes fixed on the carved lines as if weighing how they will outlive him.

dialogue.text: Rudradaman’s wars and dams belonged to his own time. But in choosing Sanskrit for this long political prose, he helped open a door where many tongues and traditions could meet and learn from one another.

i18n.hi: रुद्रदामन के युद्ध और बाँध उसी के समय के थे। पर इस लंबे राजनैतिक गद्य के लिए संस्कृत चुनकर उसने एक ऐसा द्वार खोलने में हाथ लगाया, जहाँ कई ज़बानें और परम्पराएँ मिलकर एक-दूसरे से सीख सकें।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Saka king carved Sanskrit statecraft into living stone
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक शकों राजा ने संस्कृत में राजकाज पत्थर पर उकेर दिया
